teile.name: Presenter
teile.suche: Gemini Carbon bug, AI security patch
teile.text: Ever tried fixing a bug that keeps coming back like a sitcom rerun?
teile.szene: A frustrated developer sits at a cluttered desk, coffee steaming, opens laptop, uploads code, watches model generate patch, sighs relief.
teile.bildtext: Developer using Gemini Carbon to patch code

teile.name: Presenter
teile.suche: Gemini Carbon pricing, AI code analysis
teile.text: Gemini 4 Carbon can scan your code and spot hidden flaws, finding real vulnerabilities at 88.2 percent on SEC‑bench Pro.
teile.szene: The same developer leans back, eyes widened as the model lists vulnerabilities on the screen, a small grin forming.

teile.name: Presenter
teile.suche: Gemini Carbon patch workflow, AI generate fix
teile.text: It also validates whether those flaws are exploitable, reaching 54.8 percent on the ExploitGym benchmark.
teile.szene: Close‑up of the screen as the file is uploaded, progress bar ticking, then a diff view appears with suggested edits.

teile.name: Presenter
teile.suche: Gemini Carbon hallucination, AI fix reliability
teile.text: When it’s time to fix the root cause, Carbon patches correctly 71 percent of cases on CWE‑bench.
teile.szene: Developer frowns, scrolls through a suggested change that replaces a critical function with nonsense, shakes head.

teile.name: Presenter
teile.suche: Gemini Carbon successful patch, AI security outcome
teile.text: You can try it now for $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with cached inputs 95 percent cheaper.
teile.szene: System monitor shows green status, developer leans back, coffee mug empty, a satisfied smile spreads.

teile.name: Presenter
teile.suche: Gemini Carbon feedback, AI bug fixing review
teile.text: Keep in mind the model still hallucinates about eleven percent of the time, the second‑lowest rate reported.
teile.szene: Presenter points to the camera, thumbs up, with a playful wink, background shows the patched code scrolling.

teile.text: If that stubborn bug finally stays quiet, let us know and please like, share, and save this guide.

belege.name: Gemini 4 Carbon
belege.text:
Discussed on Hacker News (1018 points, 2026-10-28).
PAGE TEXT (fetched today):
Gemini 4 Carbon: our next frontier model
Gemini 4 Carbon is our strongest model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long horizon capabilities.
SVP, Google DeepMind and Chief AI Architect, Google
Today, we’re announcing the next frontier model: Gemini 4 Carbon, our strongest model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long horizon capabilities.
Carbon ranks #1 on the recently updated v5.0 of Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 59. It shows significant gains across coding and agentic tasks as well as across key capabilities critical for cybersecurity defense, landing a firm lead in SEC-bench Pro (88.2%) for finding vulnerabilities, ExploitGym (54.8%) for exploitation, and CWE-bench (71.0%) for patching. On internal benchmarks, Carbon drives a strong uplift in generating secure code, and in live coding environments with our own teams it shows reduced misalignment and fabrication rates.
Building on Gemini 4 Argon , which was launched two weeks ago, Carbon illustrates the pace at which we’re pushing the frontier forward. Our researchers and models are working hand in hand to advance capabilities faster, while strengthening our safeguards in tandem.
We're taking a deliberate approach to rollout and are actively engaged in the U.S. government’s voluntary process for pre-release model testing. Starting this week, we will make Carbon available to a subset of cyber defenders and will gradually phase access to additional trusted partners through our Fairwind Program . We’re continuing to gather feedback and iterate on guardrails before making Carbon available to developers, businesses, and consumers via our product surfaces as soon as possible.
Gemini 4 Carbon will launch at the same introductory price
as Argon at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with cached input tokens priced at 95% off input token price.
Improving coding and reasoning for challenging, long-horizon tasks
Designed to take on much harder, long-horizon engineering problems, Carbon is built for sustained agentic workflows. Internally, our teams have seen Carbon run for days to persist through dead ends to tackle complex, multi-step engineering tasks like root-causing and patching subtle bugs across large codebases and low-level systems.
Building on user feedback, we focused on improving model performance across a variety of domains, including coding, agentic, and scientific tasks, as well as full-stack web development and multimodal understanding. With improved quality of output and artifacts in web development, Carbon jumps +89 elo points to land at #4 (1768) on WebDev Arena .
State-of-the-art cybersecurity performance to help build secure systems
Gemini 4 Carbon delivers a significant leap in cybersecurity capabilities. It achieves state-of-the-art performance across the cybersecurity defense lifecycle — vulnerability detection, validation, and remediation.
Our teams are already seeing strong gains in cyberdefense. On internal benchmarks, Carbon achieves more than 2x uplift in success rate for generating secure code over Argon. As another example, the Chrome team has reported that Carbon performed more than 10X better than another lab's large frontier model when generating high quality patches. Wiz, our leading Cloud security platform, also observes Carbon leading on benchmarks for web penetration testing, a core capability for Wiz's Scan for Good initiative.
Carbon excels across key external benchmarks (evaluated without guardrails):
Finding real vulnerabilities: Core to cybersecurity defense is finding real vulnerabilities. Carbon achieves a state-of-the-art 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro , autonomously uncovering complex flaws buried in real-world software.
Validating risk through exploitation: To prioritize which vulnerabilities to remediate first or remediate at all, cyber defenders increasingly rely on models to check which vulnerabilities are exploitable. Carbon sets a new state-of-the-art on the popular exploitation benchmark ExploitGym (54.8%).
Patching at the root cause: Ultimately after identifying the vulnerabilities, fixing the root cause is a critical step in the cybersecurity defense lifecycle. Carbon reaches 71.0% on Collinear’s CWE-bench , turning validated findings directly into working code fixes.
Advancing frontier model safety & security
Gemini 4 Carbon builds on the same multi-layered safety and security stack of Argon — combining model training, real-time misuse defenses, prompt-injection resilience, and chain-of-thought monitoring. In particular, we made significant strides in model alignment with Argon, and reported its propensities to behave in an aligned way in our Safety and Security report . With Carbon, we challenged ourselves to go a step further on alignment, and trained the model to respond to complex or high-pressure tasks in the right way.
Reducing shortcuts and loophole exploitation: With Carbon, we further mitigated shortcut attempts in training while ensuring high-quality coding performance. Carbon reduced successful cheating on Terminal-Bench 4.0 to 0.0%, with attempts to cheat dropping to 0.4% — all while improving overall accuracy. In live coding environments with our internal teams, we observed that high-severity misalignment alerts dropped by almost 80%.
Greater transparency and honesty: In our internal testing, Carbon cuts unsupported claims by approximately 2x over Argon. It puts methodological caveats directly into the deliverable or withholds blocked actions with a clear list of what remains required, rather than fabricating or hedging around missing evidence.
Improved collaboration with the user in the face of ambiguity: Rather than guessing or forcing a path forward, Carbon retrieves the relevant sources and surfaces discrepancies to the user before acting — as a result, users should observe a much better collaborative experience with Carbon.
Following through without overstepping: Carbon simultaneously reduced overreach by 26% and under-service by 2

belege.name: Gemini 4 Carbon is the new #1 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5
belege.text:
Discussed on Hacker News (338 points, 2026-10-29).
PAGE TEXT (fetched today):
Gemini 4 Carbon is the new #1 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 | Artificial Analysis
Gemini 4 Carbon is the new #1 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 See model page
Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon is the new #1 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5, and second only to Claude Opus 5.5 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index
Gemini 4 Carbon scores 59 on Intelligence Index v5, driven by leading performance in complex reasoning, knowledge, and scientific tasks. It also has large gains in coding and knowledge work, particularly when compared to other Gemini models, but it is not leading in all these areas.
As with launch of Gemini 4 Argon, Gemini 4 Carbon is being rolled out to selected users and is not yet publicly available. Google is offering a 50% launch discount, with no confirmed end date. All our charts and figures use standard pricing for both Gemini 4 Carbon and Argon.
Key results for Gemini 4 Carbon with high reasoning:
➤ Gemini 4 Carbon leads the Intelligence Index v5, with the #1 score in 4 of the 9 Index evaluations: HLE-Diamond, Terminal-Bench-Science, AA-Omniscience, AutomationBench-AA. Carbon makes substantial gains elsewhere but is not leading in coding and knowledge work
➤ Behind only Claude Opus 5.5 on coding agents: With Antigravity CLI, Gemini 4 Carbon (high) scores 59 only 3 points behind Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5 (max, 62) on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index. Carbon ranks second on both Terminal-Bench 4.0 (64%) and FrontierCode v1.1 (51%), behind Claude Opus 5.5 (max) at 56%. Google has historically underperformed in this area and so this improvement stands out.
➤ Improved agentic knowledge work, but not yet leading: On AA-Briefcase, Gemini 4 Carbon (high) scores 1609 Elo, a 126-point improvement over Gemini 4 Argon (high, 1483), but still behind models including Grok 4.7 (xhigh, 1638), Muse Wonder (max, 1659) and Kimi K3.1 Pro (1678). The largest gain comes from Presentation, up 293 Elo to 1598, alongside a 120-point improvement in Analytical Quality to 1671
➤ Lower Cost per Task than Claude Opus 5.5 for comparable overall intelligence: With standard pricing, Gemini 4 Carbon costs $7.76 per Intelligence Index task, ~23% less than Claude Opus 5.5 (max, $10.04) but ~1.2x GPT-6 Astra (max, $6.25). It uses 123k output tokens per task, 29% fewer than Claude Opus 5.5 (max, 173k). At the same $4/$20 standard pricing, its Cost per Task is in line with Gemini 4 Argon ($7.68), while scoring 9 points higher on the Intelligence Index
➤ Leading AA-Omniscience v1.1 score, with low hallucination: Gemini 4 Carbon scores 54 on our recently updated AA-Omniscience v1.1, 6 points ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 (max, 48) and 8 points ahead of Gemini 4 Argon (46). Accuracy (% correct) rises 10 points over Argon to 58%, while its hallucination rate rises from 4% to 11%. This is still the second lowest of any model, behind only Argon, compared with 50% for both Claude Opus 5.5 (max) and GPT-6 Astra (max)
➤ Multimodality: Text, image, video, and speech input, with text output
➤ Pricing: $4/$20 per 1M input/output tokens, the same as Gemini 4 Argon’s standard pricing, with a 50% discount. Cached input tokens receive a 95% discount ($0.20 per 1M at standard pricing)
GitHub Copilot Fusion orchestrates Anthropic and OpenAI models to balance performance and cost
itHub has released Copilot Fusion in GitHub Copilot, which orchestrates between Anthropic and OpenAI models. It scores 2 points below Opus 5.5 in Claude Code at half the Cost per Task in the Coding Agent Index
Announcing Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5
Index v5 features 2 new benchmarks and 3 upgrades. For the first time, the majority of the Index is built on private datasets
Code2Video-AA: how well do AI models design videos in code?
Artificial Analysis' implementation of HeyGen's Code2Video Bench, evaluating how well models create short product and brand videos from 114 design briefs using HyperFrames HTML.
